deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This is the end of Riemann's 1852 Latin fragment on the boundary behaviour (q -> root of unity) of elliptic modular functions. Dedekind later published it in Riemann's Werke as 'Fragmente über die Grenzfälle der elliptischen Modulfunctionen'. On the previous page Riemann integrated -log k', log(2K/pi), etc. against dq/q up to the boundary point q = e^{ix} (formulas 63-68). He wrote the results as series in log tan^2(px/2), log 4cos^2(px/2), and so on, plus sawtooth parts ((y)). He then specialised to x = 2*pi*m/n, starting with the imaginary part of 65.

PART A: real parts of 63 and 64 at x = 2*pi*m/n.

The real part of 63 is
 R63 = -sum_{p odd, p in Z} log tan^2(p x/2) / p^2,
which equals -2 * sum over positive odd p, since the summand is even in p. Put x/2 = m*pi/n. Then tan^2(p m pi/n) is periodic in p with period n.
- n odd: odd p are classified mod 2n. Write p = 2nt + p', with p' odd in 1..2n-1. This gives
 R63 = -sum_{p'=1,3,..,2n-1} sum_{t in Z} log tan^2(p' m pi/n) / (2nt+p')^2.
- n even: p = nt + p', with p' odd in 1..n-1, stays odd. This gives
 R63 = -sum_t sum_{p'} log tan^2(p' m pi/n) / (nt+p')^2.

Formula 64 is treated the same way with log 4cos^2(p m pi/n) in place of -log tan^2.

The inner t-sums are elementary, though Riemann does not write them out (my addition):
 sum_t 1/(Nt+p)^2 = pi^2 / (N^2 sin^2(pi p/N)).
So each limit is a finite trigonometric sum.

Bracketed remark: 63 has an infinite part unless n ≡ 0 mod 4; 64 has one when n ≡ 2 mod 4. Check, with gcd(m,n)=1 and p odd (my verification):
- tan(p m pi/n) = 0 iff n | p, possible only for n odd.
- tan(p m pi/n) = ∞ iff 2pm/n is an odd integer, i.e. n = 2d with d | p odd, i.e. n ≡ 2 mod 4.
- So log tan^2 is singular for some p exactly when n is odd or n ≡ 2 mod 4, i.e. unless 4 | n.
- cos(p m pi/n) = 0 iff n ≡ 2 mod 4.
Both claims are correct.

PART B: Abel's limit theorem.

Hypothesis (Cauchy criterion): for every eps > 0 there is n such that |a_{n+1} + ... + a_m| < eps for all m > n.

Define the shifted partial sums
 eps_{n+k} = a_{n+1} + ... + a_{n+k}.

Summation by parts gives, for 0 < r < 1,
 f(r) = sum_{k<=n} a_k r^k + sum_{j>=1} eps_{n+j} (r^{n+j} - r^{n+j+1}).
The rearrangement is legitimate because the eps_{n+j} are bounded and r^N -> 0.

Bound on the tail:
- |eps_{n+j}| < eps for all j.
- Each difference r^{n+j} - r^{n+j+1} is positive.
- Hence |tail| <= eps * sum_j (r^{n+j} - r^{n+j+1}) = eps * r^{n+1} < eps.

The head is a polynomial in r, which tends to a_0 + ... + a_n as r -> 1. Hence
 limsup_{r->1} |f(r) - (a_0+...+a_n)| <= eps.

Riemann concludes that |f(r) - S| drops below any given quantity as r -> 1, where S = sum a_k. A remark by Riemann: Dirichlet told him on 14 Sept 1852, after the above was written, that the theorem is due to Abel. The page breaks off at '...facile deducitur'. Presumably the theorem is used to justify passing to the limit q -> e^{2 pi i m/n} in the series of the previous pages.
errors: Minor gap in Part B: the step from |f(r) - (a_0+...+a_n)| < eps (eventually) to |f(r) - S| small needs |S - (a_0+...+a_n)| <= eps. This follows from the hypothesis by letting m -> ∞ (giving 2eps or 3eps overall), but Riemann leaves it implicit.
The strict inequality '< eps(r^{n+1}-r^{n+2}) + ...' should be <=. It is harmless, since eps*r^{n+1} < eps anyway for r < 1.
The positivity of r^{n+k} - r^{n+k+1} tacitly assumes 0 < r < 1 (real radial approach); this is fine for the intended use.
No mathematical errors in the reorganised double sums for 63/64 or in the finiteness criteria (n ≡ 0 mod 4 for 63, n ≢ 2 mod 4 for 64).

results.what: Boundary values at x = 2 pi m/n of Re of the integrals of -log k' dq/q and log(2K/pi) dq/q, reduced to finite sums over odd residues mod n or 2n with Hurwitz-type inner sums sum_t (Nt+p)^-2.
results.modern_name: Radial limits of Eichler-type integrals / Dedekind-eta-type logarithms at cusps; evaluation via residue classes (precursor of Dedekind-sum-type expressions)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann's fragment (1852, publ. 1876) with Dedekind's commentary; leading to Dedekind sums (Dedekind 1877)

results.what: Criterion for when the limit is infinite: 63 unless 4|n; 64 when n ≡ 2 mod 4.
results.modern_name: Behaviour of modular functions (k', K) at the cusps of Gamma(2)/Gamma_0(4)-type groups

results.what: Proof that convergence of sum a_k implies lim_{r->1-} sum a_k r^k = sum a_k, via summation by parts with tail sums eps_{n+k}.
results.modern_name: Abel's limit theorem (Abel's theorem on power series)

deep.surprise_reason: The page belongs to Riemann's 1852 fragment on the boundary cases of elliptic modular functions, published in his Werke (1876) with Dedekind's commentary. That publication includes this proof of Abel's theorem and the dated remark about Dirichlet. The residue-class reorganisation is a natural continuation of known material, and the Abel theorem proof is standard. Nothing here is new beyond what is already printed.

transcription_corrections: 'numerisatur' is probably 'nanciscatur' (obtains): '...a_m extensa, nanciscatur valorem absolutum ipso eps minorem'.
'lg lg' in 63 means log tang (log tan), as on the previous page: log tan^2(p m pi/n).
In 63/64 the index p in sum_{1,2n-1} / sum_{1,n-1} runs over odd numbers only ('designando p numerum imparem', previous page).
Bracketed remark should read: 'Formulae 63) partem habent infinitam, nisi n ≡ 0 mod 4; formula 64, si n formae est (4ν+2)'.
In the f(r) line the deleted '[-E-]' before eps_{n+1} and the corrected 'a_2 r^2' are writing corrections, not content.
'Cl.us Dirichlet' = Clarissimus Dirichlet; date reads 1852 Sept. 14.
